title: ScienceLabRunRequest/v1
description: A request to run the science lab against a ScientificClaim. This is the INPUT to the router/planner (WP-B14): it names the claim, the requested capability profiles, the resource class, and the seed/threads policy. It carries NO evidence and NO plan: prospective_holdout_materialization_allowed and status_promotion_allowed are pinned to false (a request is an intent, not an authority to materialize a holdout or promote a status), and grants_authority is pinned to false. The router produces a ScienceLabPlan/v1 from it; the plan, not the request, is what an executor consumes. Canonical JSON contract: sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8, no NaN/Infinity, trailing newline.

request_id.description: Content-addressed identity: sha256 over the canonical encoding of the request (without this field), prefixed 'sha256:'. Computed by srl.planning.request_id.

claim_id.description: The claim_id of the ScientificClaim/v1 this request targets. The router reads the claim (and its symbol_table / condition_set) to classify which capability profiles apply.

requested_profiles.description: The capability profiles the request asks to engage. Each entry MUST be one of the 15 capability profiles (see SCIENCE_LAB_PROFILES). An EMPTY array means 'auto-classify': the router runs the classifier over the claim and engages the profiles the classifier selects. A non-empty array is a request to engage exactly those profiles (the router still excludes profiles not applicable to the claim).

resource_class.description: The resource admission class: 'default' (wall 300s, rss 1.5 GiB, scratch 4 GiB) or 'exception' (wall 900s, rss 2 GiB). The planner admits a plan's summed resource estimates against the class caps; overflow raises WAIT_REMOTE_EXECUTOR (an honest wait, never a silent local substitute).

seed_policy.description: Determinism policy: a non-negative seed integer (the PRNG seed the engines MUST use) and a positive threads integer (the thread budget the engines MUST NOT exceed). Two requests byte-identical except in seed_policy produce DIFFERENT plans; two requests byte-identical INCLUDING seed_policy produce byte-identical plans (router/planner determinism).

seed.description: A non-negative integer PRNG seed. Engines consume this verbatim; it is threaded into the plan so the plan is deterministic given (request, claim, catalog, policy).

threads.description: A positive integer thread budget (>=1). Engines MUST NOT exceed this; the planner does not admit a plan whose per-step thread need exceeds it.

output_schemas.description: The schema names the request asks the run to emit (e.g. ['ScienceLabRunReceipt','EvidenceAssessment']). Carried into the plan so an executor knows what to produce. May be empty.

prospective_holdout_materialization_allo.description: Safety const: a request CANNOT authorize the materialization of a prospective holdout (data held out for out-of-sample validation). Pinned to false. A holdout may only be materialized through a separate authority path this codebase does not provide.

status_promotion_allowed.description: Safety const: a request CANNOT authorize promoting a claim's status (e.g. from under_investigation to supported). Pinned to false. Status promotion is a governance decision; the router/planner never performs it.

created_utc.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp at seconds precision (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). No offset, no fractional seconds.

canonical_writes.description: Safety const: a request is immutable once authored. Always 0; a non-zero value is a contract violation.

grants_authority.description: Safety const: a request never grants authority on its own. Always false; a true value is a contract violation. A request is an intent, not an authority.
